options.text: At most $30$ crates per hour can travel from $B$ to $T$
Exactly $30$ crates per hour travel from $B$ to $T$
options.why: Read the capacity as the amount actually flowing; the capacity is only the maximum the edge could carry.

options.text: At most $30$ crates per hour can travel between $B$ and $T$ in either direction
options.why: Ignored the arrowhead; a directed edge's capacity applies in the direction of the arrow only, and nothing may travel from $T$ to $B$.

options.text: The whole network can carry at most $30$ crates per hour
options.why: Confused one edge's capacity with the flow capacity of the entire network, which depends on every path, not on a single edge.

questions.solution_text:
The number on an edge is its capacity, the greatest amount that edge can carry each hour.
At most $30$ crates per hour can travel from $B$ to $T$, and none may travel from $T$ to $B$.
